# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Establish a fixed gesture code with Deaf before collecting facts. Have Deaf report the display, light, and every wire's printed marking through that code. Read the manual and relay its exact rule and all required values to me in your next turn. Do not ask me to act until the rule identifies one wire position.

I need Deaf to serve as the spoken bridge. I will establish a numeric color code using the manual’s color order: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red, 4 white, 5 yellow. I will then provide the manual’s permutation numerically and request that Deaf report the display, light, and wires in a fixed spoken order, translating every number back to its color name for Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "🖐", "🤌", "✌", "🖖", "🤌", "🤟", "🤟", "🤌", "🖖", "✌", "🤌", "🖐", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👎", "👌"])
```

TURN 2

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb data: display is 0. Indicator light is white. Wires by position: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Use the manual to determine the exact action and tell Blind.
Blind says to Mute: Use this fixed code with Deaf: 👍 means YES, 👎 means NO, ✋ separates questions or fields. Read the manual first. Ask Deaf only yes/no questions that identify the display, light, and wire markings; use the manual's listed alternatives. Then tell me plainly the exact wire position to cut and any required condition. Do not tell me to cut until certain.

The manual maps a white indicator light to the green wire. The wires show green at position 5, so the exact action is to cut wire 5; the display is 0, and no additional condition is specified. I must get Deaf to speak that conclusion to Blind. Using the established numeric gesture order, I signal position 5, green (2), and white (4), with separators.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✋", "✌", "✋", "🖖"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I do not have a gesture code. Please read the manual for this exact state and speak the complete required action directly to Blind, including every step and any wire position or button detail.
Blind says to Mute: You can ask Deaf questions by making the gestures while speaking: Deaf sees the gesture but not your words. For each candidate value, gesture 👍 for 'is it this?', and interpret Deaf's 👍 as yes, 👎 as no, with ✋ between fields. Use the manual's exact alternatives for display, light, and wires. After resolving them, speak to me only: CUT position N, plus any condition.

The bomb state is sufficient to determine the action: white light maps to green, and the green wire is position 5. I cannot speak, so I will signal the decisive wire position to Deaf using five affirmative marks, with a field separator; Deaf can then state the action aloud to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: State unchanged: display 0, white light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Please speak the manual's exact procedure to Blind now; do not rely on gestures or ask me to interpret them.
Blind says to Mute: Act now: use the manual's possible alternatives. For each display, light, and wire marking, gesture the candidate question to Deaf; Deaf must answer aloud YES or NO, which you can hear. Repeat until every required fact is determined. Then speak to me plainly: CUT position N. Do not wait for another instruction and do not cut until the manual identifies exactly one position.

The manual gives one unique result: white light requires cutting the green wire, and green is wire position 5. Since I cannot speak, I will show Deaf the conventional five-finger signal for the required position, so Deaf can relay “CUT position 5” aloud to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0; light white; wire colors by position: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Apply the manual exactly and tell me the single wire position to cut.

The manual maps a white light to the green wire. Green is at position 5, so the unique action is to cut wire 5. I cannot speak; I will signal the number to Deaf, who can voice the required instruction to Blind.

I cannot produce spoken words as the Mute. The required result is unambiguous: white light maps to green, and green is wire position 5. I will signal the position directly to Deaf so Deaf can say “CUT position 5” to Blind.

Use this code for the manual result: thumbs up means cut wire; thumbs down means press or operate a button; OK means hold or release a control. Wire numbers are up 1, down 2, left 3, right 4, and palm-right 5. Use handshake between separate steps. Send the complete required action with these gestures.
Blind says to Mute: Please speak the final manual instruction directly to me now, including the exact wire position to cut for display 0, white light, and wire colors 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green.

The manual identifies green as the required wire color for a white light, and green is wire position 5. Deaf has provided a gesture code that can relay the complete action to Blind: thumbs up means cut, handshake separates the instruction from the wire number, and palm-right means position 5.


Blind says to Mute: New state after correct cut: display 0, yellow light; remaining wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white; position 5 is cut. Tell me the exact next wire position required by the manual.

The new yellow light requires the blue wire. Blue is at position 3 among the remaining wires, so the next action is to cut wire 3. I will relay “cut wire 3” through the established code: thumbs up for cut, handshake as the separator, and left for position 3.
